about: Hand-labelled requirement/resume pairs. Each case states the answer a careful human reader would give, and why. Cases the tool gets wrong are kept in the file rather than deleted — the score is only worth reading if failures are allowed to show up in it.

cases.requirement: Strong Python, including async and typing
resume: Built an ingestion pipeline in Python and Pandas

cases.requirement: Working knowledge of Postgres, including query optimisation
resume: Replaced N+1 queries with batched Postgres reads
cases.why: Both say Postgres, so no keyword filter risk even though the canonical name is postgresql.

resume: Migrated a monolith to six containerised services on k8s
cases.why: k8s is Kubernetes, but the posting's own word is absent.

resume: Languages: Python, JS, TS, SQL

cases.requirement: Hands-on with Docker and Kubernetes in production
resume: Migrated six containerised services to k8s using Docker
cases.why: Docker is literal but Kubernetes is only reachable via k8s, so the requirement is still filter-fragile.

cases.requirement: Hands-on with Docker and Kubernetes in production
resume: Containerised the API with Docker
cases.why: Asks for both; only one is evidenced.
